human_tolerance.notes: Semi-aquatic; requires permanent access to freshwater and riparian food plants.

sources.title: The use of acceleration to code for animal behaviours; a case study in free-ranging Eurasian beavers Castor fiber
sources.attribution: Graf et al. (2015), PLOS ONE 10(8): e0136751, https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0136751
sources.note: The open article reports field-captured adult males (n=8, mean mass 21.7 kg) and females (n=4, mean mass 23.1 kg), and identifies walking, swimming, feeding and diving among recorded behaviors. The sexes-weighted mean is derived as (8*21.7 + 4*23.1)/12 = 22.17 kg.

sources.title: Age-related changes in somatic condition and reproduction in the Eurasian beaver: Resource history influences onset of reproductive senescence
sources.attribution: Campbell et al. (2017), PLOS ONE 12(11): e0188451, https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0188451
sources.note: Introduction states wild longevity up to 20 years and mean age at death of dominant adults about 7 years in the studied Norwegian population. This population statistic is corroborative context only and is not treated as a species-wide typical lifespan.

taxonomy.note: GBIF returned accepted species-rank Castor fiber Linnaeus, 1758; independently checked against iNaturalist taxon 43793, active at species rank.

external.note: GBIF usage key 4409131 and iNaturalist taxon 43793 resolve at their own providers to accepted/active species-rank Castor fiber; Wikidata item Q181191 also carries these identifiers.

range.note: France retains the historical Rhône remnant and the species recolonized other basins after protection and 26 reintroduction operations; country-level native status reflects the indigenous remnant, while populations are not all naturally sourced.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Study identifies walking and swimming in free-ranging Eurasian beavers.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Endotherm is the standard mammalian condition.

traits.nest_type.note: Uses bank burrows and stick-and-mud lodges.

traits.perching.note: Perching is not applicable to this quadrupedal mammal.

traits.size_class.note: 22.17 kg is below the schema's 50 kg Medium/Large boundary.

traits.mass_kg.note: Weighted mean of adult males and females captured in one Norwegian population; sample-specific, not a global adult mean.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Article gives a broad weight range of 11-30 kg.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint total length from head-body 0.80-1.00 m plus tail 0.25-0.50 m: (1.05+1.50)/2 = 1.275 m.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Midpoint (7.5 y) of ADW's explicit Typical lifespan, Status: wild, 7 to 8 years. The PLOS study reports mean age at death c. 7 y among dominant adults in one Norway population, not a species-wide average. Its up-to-20-years statement is a maximum and is excluded. ADW is the only source found that directly labels a typical wild interval; CC BY PLOS is used as context, not as a substitute statistic.

traits.diet.note: Both sources describe herbivory on woody browse and herbaceous/aquatic plants. The 0.8/0.2 browse/graze split is an authored simulation allocation, not a measured diet percentage.

traits.social.note: Wikipedia identifies monogamous pairs; ADW reports colonies up to 12. The represented group range 2-12 is a bounded synthesis of those statements.

traits.activity_pattern.note: PLOS study describes beavers as nocturnal; Wikipedia account also identifies nocturnal activity.

traits.defense.note: Flee is an authored simulation choice; sources describe territorial behavior, not a single primary defense mode.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: 0.7 for a wary, nocturnal mammal often hidden in water or its lodge.

habitat.use.note: Semi-aquatic freshwater species; ground/aquatic shares (0.2/0.8) are authored.

habitat.resources.note: Woody browse and aquatic/herbaceous plants are documented foods. Resource weights reflect the authored 0.8/0.2 simulation allocation; water, burrow and pond are placements for freshwater access and shelter.

habitat.requires.note: Freshwater habitat is required; 60 m placement radius is authored.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Conservative authored settings for a large semi-aquatic mammal; these are not measured.

seasonal.strategy.note: ADW says active throughout the year; ActiveYearRound.

seasonal.phases.note: ADW describes autumn food-cache building; Sep-Nov is an authored display window for FR.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Juvenile and adult are broad authored stages; no stage-specific durations asserted.

behavior.note: Species-local behavior is authored from documented swimming and herbivory. Swimming uses wander with the swim gait; feeding uses a separate browse eat_nearest action on land.

look.note: Block-model judgement based on brown fur, stout body, short legs and flattened broad tail; colors and proportions are authored.
